name: Din Dryfol Burial Chamber
desc: Ruined Neolithic passage-grave on a hillside ledge near Bethel, built in several phases from about 5,000 years ago - a style more usual in Ireland. In Cadw care with open access.

name: Presaddfed Burial Chambers
desc: Two Neolithic chamber tombs just north-west of Bodedern near Llyn Llywenan; the southern one still holds a 4m capstone on stout uprights. Cadw site, free access across a field.

name: Tŷ Newydd Burial Chamber
desc: Cracked 4m capstone resting on three uprights on a rock outcrop near Llanfaelog, once covered by a cairn and excavated in 1935. In Cadw care.

name: Ty Mawr Burial Chamber, Llanfairpwll
desc: A collapsed Neolithic dolmen north-east of Llanfairpwllgwyngyll whose 3.6m capstone has slipped onto its supports; a sill stone hints it was once a passage grave.

name: Pant-y-Saer Burial Chamber
desc: Partly collapsed Neolithic tomb on a scrubby hilltop above Benllech, where excavators found the remains of 56 people. The capstone now rests with one end on the ground.

name: Henblas Burial Chamber
desc: Two huge quartz-rich boulders, up to 4m tall, with a fallen 5.5m slab between them, near Llangristiolus - debated as a tomb or a natural glacial jumble.

name: Bodowyr Burial Chamber
desc: A neat little mushroom-shaped cromlech on a hillock at Bodowyr Farm east of Llangaffo, admired by antiquarian Henry Rowlands in the 1700s. Cadw site in a farmer's field, open access.

name: Perthi-Duon Burial Chamber
desc: Collapsed capstone in a field west of Brynsiencyn, drawn standing in 1723 by Henry Rowlands; some argue it is just a big boulder. Excavated in 2014.

name: Lligwy Burial Chamber
desc: Squat Neolithic tomb near Moelfre with a 25-tonne capstone on low uprights over a pit chamber; bones of 15-30 people were found in 1909. Cadw site beside the lane.

name: Trefignath Burial Chamber
desc: Three successive Neolithic chambers under one cairn on a knoll near Trearddur, Holy Island, excavated 1977-79. A line of small stones leads towards Tŷ Mawr standing stone; Cadw site.

name: Tŷ Mawr Standing Stone, Holyhead
desc: Tall Bronze Age standing stone in a field on Holy Island, a few hundred metres from Trefignath. In Cadw care.

name: Tregwehelydd Standing Stone
desc: Bronze Age standing stone in farmland near Llantrisant, Anglesey. A Cadw guardianship site.

name: Werthyr Standing Stone
desc: About 3.1m tall Bronze Age stone near Amlwch; early writers mention a second upright and a capstone that have since vanished.

name: Llanfechell Triangle Standing Stones
desc: Three standing stones set in a triangle in a field near Llanfechell, north Anglesey - an unusual prehistoric arrangement.

name: Carreg Leidr (Thief Stone)
desc: The 'thief stone' near Rhosybol: a 1.6m standing stone with a distinct hump on one side that has given rise to local folklore about a petrified thief.

name: Bedd Branwen
desc: Bronze Age burial mound by the Afon Alaw; when a cremation urn turned up in 1813 it was hailed as the grave of Branwen from the Mabinogion. Excavation in 1967 found a ring cairn, central stone and several urns.

name: Bryn Gwyn Stones
desc: The tallest standing stones in Wales, nearly 4m high, near Brynsiencyn - survivors of a ring of eight torn up by treasure-seekers in the 1790s. Cadw site.

name: Castell Bryn Gwyn
desc: Circular bank near Brynsiencyn that began as a probable Neolithic henge or sanctuary and was later refortified. Maintained by Cadw.

name: Caer Lêb
desc: Double-banked pentagonal enclosure by the Afon Braint west of Brynsiencyn, probably Iron Age with Roman-period use. Cadw site.

name: Din Lligwy Hut Group
desc: Walled late-Roman native village of round and rectangular stone huts in woods near Moelfre, where iron was worked; near Lligwy Burial Chamber. Cadw, open access.

name: Bwrdd Arthur (Din Sylwy)
desc: 'Arthur's Table' - a flat-topped limestone hill above Red Wharf Bay ringed by a stone-walled Iron Age fort, with the tiny church of St Michael beside it.

name: Parciau Hill Fort
desc: Iron Age fort on the cliff-girt summit of Bryn Ddiôl near Marian-glas, with sea views; the gentle western approach is cut off by ramparts.

name: Dinas Gynfor Hillfort
desc: Wales's most northerly hillfort, on a headland near Llanbadrig and Cemaes, partly defended by sheer cliffs.

name: Llyn Cerrig Bach
desc: Small lake near RAF Valley where over 150 Iron Age metal objects - including a slave gang-chain - were found in 1942, apparently thrown in as offerings.

name: Ffynnon Allgo
desc: Holy well of St Allgo near Llanallgo church, Moelfre, enclosed by stone walls. Scheduled monument.

name: Dinas Dinlle
desc: Coastal Iron Age fort on a glacial mound above the beach south of Caernarfon, half lost to sea erosion; linked in the Mabinogion with Lleu Llaw Gyffes.

name: Dinas Dinorwig
desc: The largest and strongest hillfort in Arfon, near Llanddeiniolen, with a stone wall inside two massive earth ramparts up to 9m high.

name: Moel y Gest hillfort
desc: Rocky 263m hill above Porthmadog crowned by an odd fort with many white quartz stones in its wall, perhaps religious rather than military. Paths from the Black Rock Sands road.

name: Carn Fadryn
desc: Iron Age hillfort enclosing the summit of a prominent Llŷn mountain, enlarged in a second phase and reused in the medieval period. Path up from Garnfadryn village.

name: Castell Odo
desc: Hillfort on Mynydd Ystum near Aberdaron whose first phases date to the late Bronze Age; legend says the giant Odo Gawr lies under a summit cairn.

name: Cefnamwlch Burial Chamber (Coetan Arthur)
desc: Neolithic burial chamber known as Coetan Arthur on Mynydd Cefnamwlch, near Tudweiliog in Llŷn.

name: Cist Cerrig Burial Chamber
desc: Remains of a Neolithic burial chamber near Garndolbenmaen with a cup-marked rock nearby.

name: Ystum Cegid Burial Chamber
desc: Neolithic chambered long cairn near Llanystumdwy, between Criccieth and Porthmadog.

name: Bachwen Burial Chamber
desc: Small Neolithic dolmen on the coast at Clynnog Fawr whose capstone is covered in cup-marks.

name: Penarth Burial Chamber
desc: Neolithic chamber tomb in fields near Clynnog Fawr, part of the cluster of tombs on this coast.

name: Llyn Ogwen
desc: Shallow lake beside the A5 below Tryfan; legend says Sir Bedivere threw Excalibur here after Camlann and that Tryfan is his resting place.

name: Llyn Idwal
desc: Glacial lake in Cwm Idwal named after Prince Idwal Foel, whose son legend says was drowned here. Popular circular path from Ogwen.

name: Maen Llwyd, Glynllifon
desc: Bronze Age standing stone in the Glynllifon area near Llandwrog.

name: Dyffryn Ardudwy Burial Chamber
desc: Two Neolithic portal tombs in one long cairn behind the village school, among the earliest tombs in Britain (c.4000 BC). In Cadw care, open access.

name: Carneddau Hengwm
desc: Two great Neolithic long cairns on the hillside above Dyffryn Ardudwy, with remains of chambers; reached on foot by an upland track.

name: Cors-y-Gedol Burial Chamber
desc: Neolithic chamber with a sloping capstone amid ancient field walls near Dyffryn Ardudwy, with views over Cardigan Bay.

name: Hengwm Stone Circles
desc: Pair of prehistoric stone circles on the moorland above Dyffryn Ardudwy, near the Carneddau Hengwm cairns.

name: Bryn Cader Faner
desc: Bronze Age cairn east of Talsarnau ringed by 18 slanting slate spikes like a crown, dating to the late 3rd millennium BC. Damaged by army gunnery; a remote moorland walk.

name: Moel Goedog cairns and stones
desc: Bronze Age ring cairns and standing stones along an ancient trackway near Harlech, below Moel Goedog hillfort.

name: Llech Idris
desc: Leaning 3.1m Bronze Age slab near Trawsfynydd; folklore says the giant Idris hurled it from Cadair Idris.

name: Cerrig Arthur Stone Circle
desc: Small embanked stone circle on the hills above Barmouth, bearing King Arthur's name.

name: Eglwys Gwyddelod Stone Circle
desc: The 'Irishmen's church' - a small stone circle on the uplands above Tywyn.

name: Llynnau Cregennen Standing Stone
desc: Standing stone near the Cregennen lakes below Cadair Idris, National Trust land with a car park and walks.

name: Craig yr Aderyn
desc: Bird Rock, a 258m crag in the Dysynni valley and the largest inland cormorant colony in Wales; its top carries a two-phase Iron Age fort.

name: Caer Euni
desc: Long narrow Iron Age fort on a 365m ridge north-east of Llandderfel near Bala, with its main entrance at the north-east end.

name: Llyn Barfog
desc: 'Bearded Lake' above Aberdyfi, home in legend to the afanc that Arthur dragged out, and to green-clad fairies with white cattle. Reached by a hill path.

name: Carn March Arthur
desc: Stone near Llyn Barfog bearing a hoof-shaped hollow, said to be the print of Arthur's horse as it hauled the afanc from the lake. Marked by a slate sign.

name: Dolgoch Falls
desc: Series of three waterfalls in a wooded gorge near Tywyn, reached on foot from Dolgoch station on the Talyllyn Railway.

name: Capel Garmon Burial Chamber
desc: Severn-Cotswold style long cairn above Betws-y-Coed with a passage and twin chambers, one still roofed by its capstone; once used as a stable. Cadw site.

name: Maen y Bardd
desc: Classic little Neolithic dolmen beside the old track near Rowen; its names mean 'bard's stone', 'shepherd's hut' and 'greyhound's kennel'.

name: Llety'r Filiast, Great Orme
desc: Neolithic chambered tomb on the Great Orme near the tramway; the name means 'lair of the greyhound bitch'.

name: Hwylfa'r Ceirw
desc: Stone alignment on the Great Orme whose name means 'the deer's track'.

name: Kendrick's Cave
desc: Great Orme cave where lapidary Thomas Kendrick found a decorated horse jaw, bear-tooth beads and human bones in 1880 - some of Britain's oldest art.

name: Ogof Tan-y-Bryn
desc: Palaeolithic cave at Llandudno, protected as a scheduled monument.

name: Bwlch y Ddeufaen standing stones
desc: The 'pass of the two stones': twin prehistoric standing stones on the old Roman road over the Carneddau between Rowen and Abergwyngregyn. Walkable green track.

name: Cerrig Pryfaid Stone Circle
desc: Small stone circle on the moors near Bwlch y Ddeufaen, above Rowen.

name: Maen Crwn and Bryn Derwydd Circle
desc: A standing stone and small stone circle on the Penmaenmawr uplands, part of the ritual landscape around the Druid's Circle.

name: Allor Moloch (Hendre-Waelod)
desc: Dolmen with a huge capstone beside a footpath overlooking the Conwy estuary near Llansanffraid Glan Conwy.

name: Castell Caer Seion
desc: Iron Age fort on top of Conwy Mountain containing a smaller, more heavily defended fort within it; occupied from about the 6th century BC.

name: Caer Bach
desc: Small fort on a hillock on the eastern slopes of Tal-y-Fan above Rowen, little investigated.

name: Bryn Euryn
desc: Hill above Rhos-on-Sea with a massive limestone-walled hillfort on top and the ruin of Llys Euryn below; local nature reserve.

name: Castell Cawr
desc: Wooded hill above Abergele (Tan-y-Gopa) with an Iron Age fort and caves used by rare lesser horseshoe bats; Woodland Trust land.

name: Pen-y-Corddyn
desc: Large limestone hillfort above Llanddulas, near Abergele.

name: Pen y Dinas, Great Orme
desc: Small hillfort on the Great Orme above Llandudno.

name: Fairy Falls, Trefriw
desc: Falls about 25 feet high on the Afon Crafnant in Trefriw village, left by Ice Age glaciers that cut the side valley short.

name: Rhaeadr y Parc Mawr, Llanrwst
desc: Waterfall, nicknamed the Grey Mare's Tail, just off the B5106 near Gwydir Castle, fed by a stream running out of the Gwydir Forest mines.

name: Llyn Geirionydd
desc: Lake in the Gwydir Forest linked to the bard Taliesin, with a memorial to him by the water; the lane comes from Trefriw or Llanrwst.

name: St George's Well, Abergele
desc: Early medieval holy well at St George near Abergele, once used to bless horses. Scheduled monument.

name: Bedd-y-Cawr Hillfort
desc: 'The Giant's Grave' - an Iron Age promontory fort at the end of the Cefn Meiriadog ridge west of St Asaph, over the Elwy valley.

name: Cefn Caves
desc: Four linked caves in limestone cliffs above the Elwy, where Palaeolithic tools and animal bones were dug out from the 1830s. Reached on a woodland path.

name: Cae Gwyn Cave, Tremeirchion
desc: Valley-side caves above the Vale of Clwyd where stone tools were found with mammoth and woolly rhino bones in the 1880s.

name: Moel y Gaer, Bodfari
desc: Lowest of the Clwydian Range chain of hillforts, on a 200m summit over the Wheeler valley near Bodfari.

name: Moel y Gaer, Llanbedr
desc: Oval Iron Age fort on a western spur of the Clwydian Range above Llanbedr Dyffryn Clwyd, overlooking the Vale.

name: Moel y Gaer, Llantysilio
desc: Iron Age fort on Llantysilio Mountain north-west of Llangollen, part of the Heather and Hillforts project.

name: Moel Hiraddug
desc: Hillfort above Dyserth at the north end of the Clwydian Range, partly quarried away; wide views to Snowdonia.

name: Maen Huail
desc: Stone block in St Peter's Square, Ruthin, on which King Arthur is said to have beheaded Huail, brother of Gildas.

name: Bryn Beddau Stone Circle
desc: Circle of at least 19 stones in a heather clearing in Clocaenog Forest, near the fallen 3.4m Maen Llwyd.

name: Tyfos Stone Circle
desc: Bronze Age kerb circle of thirteen fallen stones near Llandrillo in the Dee valley.

name: Tyddyn Bleiddyn Burial Chamber
desc: Two Neolithic cairns at Cefn Meiriadog dug in the mid-1800s, revealing crouched burials in stone cists.

name: Horseshoe Falls, Llangollen
desc: Curving Telford weir on the Dee above Llangollen that feeds the canal; a short walk from Berwyn station.

name: The Gop
desc: Huge Neolithic cairn on Gop Hill above Trelawnyd, the second-largest prehistoric mound in Britain after Silbury Hill; caves below held Neolithic burials.

name: Maen Achwyfan
desc: Tallest wheel-headed cross in Britain (3.4m), carved around the 11th century and standing in a field near Whitford. Cadw site.

name: Penbedw Stone Circle
desc: Five stones in a ring completed by oaks in Penbedw Park near Nannerch - possibly an 18th-century folly - with a genuine Bronze Age standing stone nearby.

name: Carreg-y-llech
desc: 1.9m Bronze Age standing stone near Treuddyn, possibly once set in a burial mound.

name: Caer Estyn
desc: Hillfort on a ridge near Hope above the Alyn valley.

name: Thor's Stone, Thurstaston
desc: Great red sandstone outcrop on Thurstaston Common; folklore makes it a Viking altar to Thor or a stone he hurled, and children once danced round it.

name: Bidston Hill rock carvings
desc: Sandstone carvings of a sun goddess and a horse near Bidston Observatory, thought to be Norse-Irish work of around AD 1000; the goddess faces midsummer sunrise.

name: The Calder Stones
desc: Six Neolithic sandstone slabs with cup-and-ring and spiral carvings from a lost burial monument, now displayed at Calderstones Park, Liverpool.

name: Robin Hood's Stone, Allerton
desc: Bronze Age cup-marked standing stone at Booker Avenue, Liverpool; its grooves are said to come from archers sharpening arrows.

name: Bickerton Hill Iron Age fort
desc: Iron Age fort known as Maiden Castle on Bickerton Hill, on the Sandstone Trail, one of only seven in Cheshire; National Trust heathland.

name: Kelsborrow Castle
desc: Iron Age promontory fort near Kelsall, part of a small cluster with Eddisbury; a bronze palstave was found here.

name: The Devil's Chair, Stiperstones
desc: Largest of the shattered quartzite tors on the Stiperstones ridge, steeped in Devil folklore; Wild Edric is said to ride here when England is threatened.

name: The Wrekin hillfort
desc: Iron Age fort on the 407m summit of the Wrekin; legend says the hill is earth dropped by a giant who meant to bury Shrewsbury.

name: Hoarstones
desc: Oval circle of low stones near Chirbury, one of only two surviving circles in this border area with Mitchell's Fold.

name: Bury Ditches
desc: Spectacular oval multi-ramparted Iron Age fort on Sunnyhill between Clun and Bishop's Castle, managed by Forestry England with a car park nearby.

name: Nordy Bank
desc: Single-ramparted late Bronze Age/early Iron Age fort on a spur of Brown Clee Hill.

name: Titterstone Clee hillfort
desc: Iron Age fort on the 533m summit of Titterstone Clee, unusual for its stone-block walls, alongside Bronze Age cairns and old quarries.

name: Doll Tor
desc: Small six-stone circle just west of Stanton Moor near Birchover; on private farmland with no public access.

name: Nine Stones Close (Grey Ladies)
desc: Four tall survivors of a circle on Harthill Moor near Elton, one with cup marks, close to Robin Hood's Stride.

name: Robin Hood's Stride
desc: Gritstone outcrop with two pinnacles, also called Mock Beggar's Mansion, beside the old Portway near Elton; a medieval crucifix is carved in the nearby Hermit's Cave.

name: Andle Stone
desc: Big cup-and-ring marked boulder on Stanton Moor, later inscribed to the Duke of Wellington; on private land.

name: Barbrook One
desc: Embanked stone circle among about 80 cairns on Ramsley Moor near Baslow.

name: Wet Withens
desc: Largest embanked stone circle in Derbyshire, on Eyam Moor; off the paths but on open-access land.

name: Hordron Edge (Seven Stones)
desc: Bronze Age circle on Moscar Moor above Ladybower reservoir, known as the Seven Stones of Hordron.

name: Five Wells Chambered Tomb
desc: High Neolithic tomb on Taddington Moor with two paved chambers; at least twelve skeletons were found here.

name: Minninglow
desc: Tree-capped hill near Pikehall holding Derbyshire's largest Neolithic chambered tomb and two Bronze Age barrows.

name: Gib Hill
desc: Big barrow 300m from Arbor Low, a Neolithic oval mound topped by a Bronze Age round barrow with a cremation cist.

name: Hob Hurst's House
desc: Unusual square Bronze Age barrow on Beeley Moor above Chatsworth; English Heritage guardianship, beside the moorland walk.

name: Carl Wark
desc: Cliff-girt promontory on Hathersage Moor walled off by an ancient rampart, often read as an Iron Age fort though its date is uncertain.

name: Fin Cop
desc: Hillfort above Monsal Dale, hastily built; excavations in 2011 found a mass grave of women and children from a massacre.

name: Poole's Cavern
desc: Limestone show cave on the edge of Buxton named after a 15th-century outlaw; Bronze Age and Roman-period finds came from inside.

name: Blue John Cavern
desc: Castleton show cave where the rare banded Blue John stone is still mined in small amounts; guided tours.

name: Cucklet Church, Eyam
desc: Rock arch in the Delph at Eyam where the rector held open-air services during the 1665 plague; a commemoration service is still held there.

name: Doxey Pool, The Roaches
desc: Small pool on top of the Roaches said to hold a water spirit or mermaid, sometimes called Jenny Greenteeth, who lures walkers in.

name: Speedwell Cavern
desc: Castleton cave reached by boat along a flooded miners' level to a cavern with a 'Bottomless Pit' and underground lake.

name: Pikestones
desc: Neolithic chambered long cairn on Anglezarke Moor above Chorley, with the slabs of its burial chamber still visible.

name: Round Loaf
desc: Large prehistoric round barrow on Anglezarke Moor, lined up between Great Hill and Pikestones.

name: Heysham rock-cut graves
desc: Body-shaped graves cut into the headland rock beside the ruined Saxon St Patrick's Chapel at Heysham.

name: Warton Crag
desc: Limestone hill near Carnforth topped by a small multi-ramparted hillfort; nature reserves with views over Morecambe Bay.

name: Castercliff
desc: Iron Age hillfort with triple ramparts on a hill between Nelson and Colne.

name: Cheetham Close
desc: Damaged stone circle on moorland near Turton, smashed by a farmer in the 1870s; once claimed as a druid site.

name: Birkrigg Stone Circle
desc: Double ring of stones on Birkrigg Common south of Ulverston, known as the Druids' Temple; cremations were found under its cobbles.

name: Burnmoor Stone Circles
desc: Five circles on the moor above Boot in Eskdale, the largest (Brat's Hill) holding five cairns; National Trust.

name: Elva Plain Stone Circle
desc: Large widely spaced circle on Elva Hill north of Bassenthwaite Lake, reached by footpath from the road.

name: Grey Croft Stone Circle
desc: Restored circle of twelve stones near Seascale, close to Sellafield, re-erected after being buried by a farmer in 1820.

name: Kinniside Stone Circle
desc: Small granite circle beside the fell road from Ennerdale Bridge, 'restored' in concrete in 1925.

name: Little Meg
desc: Kerb circle near Long Meg with one stone carved with concentric rings and a spiral.

name: Gamelands Stone Circle
desc: Oval of fallen pink granite stones near Orton, partly blasted in 1862.

name: King Arthur's Round Table
desc: Neolithic henge at Eamont Bridge near Penrith, its Arthurian name long attached; free English Heritage site.

name: Mayburgh Henge
desc: Massive Neolithic henge with banks of river cobbles and a lone standing stone inside, near Eamont Bridge; English Heritage, free.

name: Giant's Grave, Black Combe
desc: Two standing stones with cup-and-ring marks at the foot of Black Combe, in a field off the A595.

name: Dog Hole Cave (Fairy Cave)
desc: Shaft cave near Storth, also called the Fairy Cave, where excavations found prehistoric human and animal remains.

name: Heaning Wood Bone Cave
desc: Cave at Great Urswick with burials from the Neolithic and Bronze Age and human bone dated to about 11,000 years ago.

name: Carrock Fell hillfort
desc: Oval stone-walled Iron Age fort crowning Carrock Fell in the northern Lake District.

name: Castle Crag
desc: Small craggy Borrowdale fell whose summit is thought to have been an ancient hillfort, partly quarried away.

name: Scale Force
desc: The Lake District's highest waterfall, about 170 feet, hidden in a gorge on Red Pike above Crummock Water.

name: Lodore Falls
desc: Cascade from Watendlath tumbling into Borrowdale near Derwentwater, possibly the Derwennydd falls of an old Welsh lullaby.

name: Taylor Gill Force
desc: One of the Lake District's highest falls, in Seathwaite above Borrowdale.

name: Cautley Spout
desc: England's highest cascade above ground, falling 650 feet from the Howgill Fells near Sedbergh.

name: Popping Stone, Gilsland
desc: Boulders in the Irthing Gorge famous for marriage proposals, where Walter Scott is said to have proposed in 1797.
